transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Well, what brought me in is that people keep saying I’m not listening to them. My supervisor at work, or my wife... they'll be talking straight to me, and then a minute later I realize I only caught about half of it. I end up having to ask them to say it all over again. It's been causing some problems, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to somebody.
Did you have similar difficulties paying attention when you were a child in school?

Yeah, I was like this even back then. Honestly, teachers were always moving my seat around because I just couldn’t stay put in my chair. I used to call out answers all the time without raising my hand, and I got into trouble a lot for... well, for butting into other kids’ work. This was all way back before middle school. So, yeah, it's been going on a long time.
Nowadays, do you still find yourself feeling restless or having a hard time sitting still?

Yeah, I do. It's actually pretty bad. If I have to just sit there, it starts feeling like... like this pressure is just building up inside my chest and my legs. It gets to the point where I feel like I have to move or do something right that second, or I'm just going to crawl right out of my skin.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms significant ongoing adult hyperactivity and inner restlessness in addition to inattentive symptoms and childhood onset of both, ruling out predominantly inattentive type (F90.0).
